summary: Yes. cache.py:20 'if self.clock() - stored > self.ttl' is strict, so an entry aged exactly ttl is still served; it expires only when strictly older (deleted lazily at cache.py:21 on get). Observed with injected clock, ttl=10: age 9.999 -> v, 10 -> v, 10.001 -> MISS. Why: commit 7c6352a 'Keep cache entries through their last second (#12)' changed '>=' to '>' (97e4961 originally used >=): on coarse clocks (monotonic ticking in 15 ms steps) ttl=1 entries expired on first read after a one-tick advance; the message says ttl should be the minimum lifetime callers can rely on. Rationale is stated in the commit message (direct), not inferred.
